channel.title: FuseZap blog
channel.description: Notes from the work: what we measured, what was slow, what we changed and what still isn’t done.

item.title: What to have ready before your chip’s first model
item.description: The list in your head before bring-up is long. The list we ask for is short: a toolchain that can do three things, one engineer who knows it, and your customers’ models.

item.title: Three tests out of 1,174
item.description: Our first week on Inferentia2, a chip we didn’t design: the simulator first, one backend, a 22-minute run with three failures, and a first model that was slow and right.

item.title: Every check but one
item.description: In October, Validate passed a popular 70B model on accuracy and reliability, then blocked it: its tool calls sent numbers as text. Why one red gate was the right call.

item.title: Five milliseconds we didn’t take
item.description: On Inferentia2 a faster setting would have put our first token level with AWS’s library. It wasn’t bit for bit, so we shipped the exact one.

item.title: The mountain is smaller than it looks
item.description: A cloud’s models page can feel like a verdict on your chip. Underneath sit a handful of model families. We climbed the first one on a chip we didn’t design.

item.title: Catching up with vLLM, then a chip that isn’t a GPU
item.description: How FuseZap went from well behind vLLM to level on one NVIDIA GPU in October 2026, what the NCCL surprise was on two GPUs, and our first run on a real AWS Inferentia2.
